Transcript body:
[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining—uh—good to see Nimbus team. Quick intros, we'll do a 30-ish minute demo and then dive into the migration parity mapping Q&A and pilot planning.
[00:18] Aisha: Hi all, thanks. We just want to make sure we can replace our OpenAI/Anthropic calls without regression, and also check dedicated/private options. Security is a big driver.
[00:30] Eric: Great. Quick outline: we'll show Redwood API parity, Console for routing/rollouts, and Optimize recommendations for batching/quantization. Then open Q&A and next steps.
[00:42] Marcus: For context, we run both GPT-4 via OpenAI and Claude/Anthropic for some safety-checking flows, and Together models for embeddings. Latency targets are 300ms p95 for short chats, and embeddings are batch throughput focused.
[01:05] Priya: Noted. One thing to call out—Redwood's parity layer maps standard OpenAI-style params but there are subtle differences in streaming/chunk events and function-calling semantics; we'll show the mapping doc.
[01:20] Oliver: Are there breaking format changes? We have a couple of infra teams that will have to update code.
[01:28] Sofia: Good question. In most cases it's minimal: same request/response structures, keys named similarly, but we do have model name mappings, and some optional fields—like Redwood's route and priority headers—are new. We'll include compatibility snippets.
[01:45] (screen share starts)
[02:00] Eric: Ok pulling up the parity mapping slide—so, left column is OpenAI parameters, middle is Anthropic/Together equivalents, right is Redwood API example. For example, openai's "max_tokens" maps to "max_tokens" with Redwood, Anthropic has a different default so watch the temperature mapping.
[02:25] Marcus: Quick transcription note—our safety wrappers rely on function calling behavior. Does Redwood support function/tool calling exactly like OpenAI?
[02:35] Priya: We support function calling and structured output. There can be differences in how streaming emits the arguments; sometimes the model libraries chunk them differently. We include a small shim in the SDK to normalize.
[02:50] Aisha: Security: are logs encrypted and do you support KMS?
[02:56] Sofia: Yes: KMS integration supported for Private, and for Dedicated we offer customer-managed keys; hosted has BYOK options for enterprise. Audit logs and retention policies are configurable. We'll send the security pack after the call.
[03:12] Oliver: What about SOC2 and ISO certs?
[03:16] Sofia: We have SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 — we'll attach certs.
[03:25] Eric: Now switching to Console—this is the per-route dashboard. You can pin model versions, set rollouts (canary / A/B), and see token-level cost breakdown. For migration that's helpful to route a % of traffic to Redwood while falling back to OpenAI if mismatch.
[03:45] Marcus: Do you do automatic fallback between model families, like if capacity tight?
[03:50] Eric: Yes, smart routing policies let you fallback to cheaper model variants or to another region; you set compatibility constraints in the route config.
[04:05] (brief crosstalk)
[04:20] Priya: Next, Optimize—this recommends batching sizes and quantization profiles by workload. For your embedding jobs we saw significant savings by batching to 256 vectors and enabling prefix caching for repeated customer prompts.
[04:40] Aisha: Marcus, do we have sample volumes for embeddings?
[04:44] Marcus: We're at ~20k embeddings/day with bursts to 100k during reindex. Latency during reindex needs to be high throughput; background batch OK.
[05:02] Eric: That fits a Dedicated or Private capacity model. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and surge options; Private if you need full on-premise. Tradeoffs: Dedicated much simpler to start, Private requires infra work (VPC peering or air-gapped depending).
[05:20] Sofia: Let's demo an example API call. We'll show an OpenAI-style call and the Redwood equivalent, plus an SDK snippet.
[05:30] (typing, demo)
[05:50] Eric: Example 1: OpenAI chat completion with function calling. Here's your current payload—(reads) role system, messages array, functions. On Redwood, same top-level shape; we add an optional "route" header and the model name mapping, e.g., openai:gpt-4 -> redwood:gpt4-rlhf-v1 (internal alias).
[06:12] Marcus: How do you handle KV-cache across streams? We're very latency sensitive for multi-turn where KV cache warms up.
[06:20] Priya: Redwood's runtime exposes KV cache behavior and supports prefix/KV caching. For migration we can preserve prefixes and ensure the same cache keys are used. There's also a sticky routing option so subsequent messages hit the same instance to warm cache.
[06:40] Aisha: Any implications for conversational context length? Our longest threads are ~12k tokens in customer support cases.
[06:48] Eric: We support variable sequence lengths; recommendation is to shard long context as embeddings and use relevance windows. For native support, we have model variants tuned for long context and the runtime picks kernels accordingly.
[07:05] Oliver: Cost question: how does unit cost compare to OpenAI?
[07:10] Sofia: It depends—hosted API pricing roughly maps to per-token but we often see lower token cost with similar latency when using Dedicated or optimized quantized variants. Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization profiles for your workload to reduce token op cost. We'll provide a cost model after the demo.
[07:30] Marcus: For Together embeddings, how is vector similarity parity? Small differences in vectors can change nearest-neighbor results.
[07:38] Priya: We try to provide the same model semantics; for embeddings we map Together's model to a Redwood-verified variant. We also recommend running a calibration eval (50-200 samples) to measure drift. If there's drift we can recommend re-ranking or hybrid approach during pilot.
[07:56] (screen: live code editor)
[08:10] Eric: Showing SDK snippet—old code calling openai.Chat.create... new call is redwood.chat.create with identical params in most cases. There's a small helper in our SDK: redwood.migrate.from_openai(payload) that rewrites function payloads and streaming events.
[08:30] Marcus: That's helpful. Do you have examples for Anthropic -> Redwood? Their tokenization and prompt framing is different.
[08:37] Priya: Yes, Anthropic tends to use different system message patterns and safety templates. Our parity doc includes recommended prompt rewrites and a mapping table of system token adjustments. We'll drop that in the parity mapping doc.
[08:55] Aisha: Pilot logistics — we need to test both hosted and Dedicated paths. Our security team prefers Private but infra bandwidth is limited. Can we start hosted and then move to Dedicated?
[09:05] Sofia: Absolutely. Most customers start hosted for quick validation, then move to Dedicated when they need throughput/SLA or Private for compliance. We support pinning model versions across modes so code changes are minimal.
[09:22] Marcus: About fallbacks—if we route 10% of traffic to Redwood, failure should fallback to OpenAI automatically. How do you instrument that?
[09:30] Eric: We have per-request tracing and per-route policies. If Redwood returns a heavy latency or error, an automatic fallback to a configured upstream happens within a policy window. You can tune retry and fallback thresholds.
[09:50] (customer question)
[10:00] Oliver: Do we need to change data retention / GDPR processes? We have PHI concerns for health data.
[10:08] Sofia: For PHI you likely need Private or strict Dedicated contracts with data isolation and specific retention rules. For hosted, we offer enterprise contracts with data handling addendums but for PHI-compliant workloads Private or on-prem is recommended. We do offer BAA discussions.
[10:25] Aisha: Good—please flag BAA as part of the security pack.
[10:30] (demo continues)
[11:00] Eric: Now, a short benchmark example—this is a synthetic p95 latency chart from a Nearby customer migrating from OpenAI. You can see comparable p50/p95 when using a quantized variant and tuned batching; p95 got from 420ms to 310ms.
[11:25] Marcus: Can you share the raw benchmark spreadsheets and test harness?
[11:30] Eric: Yes will share; it's in the next steps. We recommend running a 2-week pilot with your real traffic for reliable numbers.
[11:45] Priya: A note about embeddings reindexing: we suggest doing initial reindex on Dedicated with burst capacity and then switch to batch windows to smooth cost. Optimize can automate batching windows.
[12:05] (15 minute mark: pause for questions)
[12:25] Aisha: How much engineering time do you expect to migrate the existing prompt flows?
[12:32] Sofia: For most customers it's a few sprints of minor SDK fixes and prompt tuning—maybe 2-4 engineers part-time for 3-6 weeks depending on integration depth. The parity doc and SDK helpers reduce effort.
[12:50] Marcus: Any gotchas with model fine-tuning or custom models? We sometimes use fine-tuned Anthropic variants.
[12:58] Priya: If you have custom fine-tunes, we can host model variants in Dedicated/Private; for parity we map to the closest public variant and run evals. Fine-tunes require model onboarding.
[13:20] (customer asks about billing granularity)
[13:30] Sofia: Billing is per-token for hosted, with per-hour reserved capacity for Dedicated, and licensing/support for Private. You get token-level cost breakdowns in Console to attribute to product routes.
[13:50] Oliver: For Dedicated, what's the SLA?
[13:55] Eric: Dedicated has an SLA with uptime and latency targets—details in the SLA doc. For Private we offer enterprise SLAs in contracts.
[14:10] (minor transcript noise; auto-captions errors: "Redwood" sometimes transcribed as "Red wood")
[14:30] Marcus: Ok we want to run two pilots: embeddings heavy reindex (batch) and chat latency sensitive flow.
[14:38] Sofia: Sounds good. We'll propose a pilot plan: week 0 onboarding, week 1-2 pilot run, evaluation at end with parity metrics.
[14:50] Aisha: Parity metrics—what do you measure?
[14:55] Eric: We'll measure latency (p50/p95), token cost, semantic similarity for embeddings (recall@k), and safety/regression on sample evals. Also end-to-end error rates and fallback frequency.
[15:15] Marcus: Any automation to block regressions on prompt changes?
[15:20] Priya: Yes, Redwood Optimize supports eval suites and regression alerts tied to prompt sets; you can run nightly evals against a baseline.
[15:35] (discussion of network setup)
[15:45] Oliver: For Private we need VPC peering or direct connect options—what do you support?
[15:50] Sofia: VPC peering, VPN, and dedicated interconnects are supported depending on customer infra. For air-gapped on-prem we ship an appliance or a container package.
[16:10] Aisha: Great. Please include network checklist in runbook.
[16:15] (demo wrapping)
[16:30] Eric: Quick notes on quantization: for chat we tested 8-bit quantized variants that retained quality for many workloads; Optimize recommends profile based on evals. There's a tradeoff so we suggest running small AB test.
[16:50] Marcus: For the SDK, do we need to run new dependencies?
[16:55] Priya: Minimal—our SDK is drop-in compatible with OpenAI client in many languages. There's an adapter shim. We'll provide sample code.
[17:10] Aisha: Any enterprise legal points—data residency in EU? We're in US/EU with some EU patient data.
[17:18] Sofia: We have regions in EU and US, and for Private you can keep all data in your VPC. We'll mark data residency controls in the security pack.
[17:35] (client asks about observability)
[17:45] Eric: Console has per-route metrics, traces, token breakdown, and error analysis. You can hook in tracing to Datadog or internal tracing.
[17:58] Marcus: Great. Ok what's the next step timeline?
[18:05] Sofia: We'll send the parity doc and security pack by end of week, benchmark spreadsheet and pilot proposal early next week, and propose pilot kickoff week of 10/06.
[18:18] Aisha: Sounds good. Also we need price estimate for Dedicated vs Hosted for the pilot.
[18:25] Sofia: We'll include pricing; note Dedicated has committed pricing and burst options.
[18:40] (closing Q&A)
[18:50] Oliver: One small question—how are rate limits handled during reindex? We don't want background jobs to disrupt chat SLOs.
[18:58] Eric: You can set route-level quotas and priority classes; Optimize can schedule embedding batches during off-peak windows and limit concurrency so chat routes don't suffer.
[19:15] Marcus: Ok perfect.
[19:20] (wrap-up)
[19:30] Sofia: Recap: we'll send parity mapping doc, security pack (SOC2/ISO/KMS/BAA note), benchmark spreadsheet, and pilot plan. Action items and owners will be in the follow-up. Pilot target week of 10/06.
[19:50] Aisha: Thanks everyone, look forward to the docs.
